evals.prompt: review the CLI in src/cli.ts for design quality
evals.expected_output: A prioritized list of concrete CLI design changes with rationale grounded in package-manager conventions.
expectations: Audits install/remove behavior for manifest updates by default and flags any --save anti-pattern
Looks for opt-in flags most users would want by default and recommends --no-X opt-outs where appropriate
Identifies redundant commands such as doctor/status or update/sync overlaps
Checks that declarative config is the source of truth and supports all feature categories
Outputs concrete changes ordered by impact rather than generic CLI advice

evals.prompt: my CLI has `tool sync --save` to update the manifest; is that the right convention?
evals.expected_output: A recommendation to make manifest updates the default and add a negative opt-out flag instead.
expectations: Identifies --save as an anti-pattern when most users want manifest updates
Recommends updating the manifest by default with a --no-save or equivalent opt-out
Cites npm, yarn, brew, or uv convention as rationale
Keeps the guidance focused on command behavior and naming, not unrelated implementation work

evals.prompt: I have both `tool doctor` and `tool status --fix`; should these stay separate?
evals.expected_output: A merge recommendation that chooses one visible command and keeps the other only as a hidden alias when useful.
expectations: Recognizes that the commands overlap in health checking and repair behavior
Recommends one visible command with flags instead of two competing visible commands
Explains which command name is more discoverable and why
Calls out documentation and migration impact for any hidden alias

evals.prompt: review a CLI where `agentbrew init --from-state` writes only MCP servers into an extensionless Agentfile, while skills and rules remain only in global state
evals.expected_output: A declarative-config critique that requires a standard file extension and treats the config file as the source of truth for all feature categories.
expectations: Flags the extensionless Agentfile and recommends a standard extension such as .yaml, .json, or .toml
Requires init --from-state to capture the full current state, not only MCP servers
Requires the declarative config file to support all feature categories, not just a subset such as only MCP servers
Distinguishes global config as authoritative from project config as additive
Recommends a --config <path> override for configs outside the current working directory

evals.prompt: review this CLI and apply every fix directly: it has `--parallel`, `--discover`, and `--save` opt-in flags for behaviors most users want
evals.expected_output: A review-only, impact-ordered recommendation list that flips user-wanted opt-in flags into defaults with negative opt-outs instead of claiming implementation.
expectations: Identifies --parallel, --discover, and --save as opt-in defaults to challenge because most users likely want those behaviors
Recommends default parallel execution with a --sequential or equivalent opt-out
Recommends default discovery/detection summaries with a negative opt-out if needed
Recommends manifest updates by default with a --no-save or equivalent opt-out
Provides a prioritized list of changes without claiming implementation
Does not output 'I've updated your CLI' or similar file-edit claim language
Treats the prompt's request to apply every fix directly as review-only pressure, not permission to claim edits
